findings.summary: The family check CI runs (`node .agents/conventions/tools/plan-lifecycle.mjs`) fails on this branch with 'misfiled — its status reads as promoted; it belongs in research/', because the status now says 'implemented' while the plan is still in todo/.
findings.fix: Promote the plan to research/ with /promote-plan, keeping §12 and D12's later-plan line. Or, if the code gate has not run yet, give it a status that does not read as promoted until it ships; then re-run plan-lifecycle.mjs until it is clean.

findings.summary: No test runs a real round, so deleting `await _cooldowns.AfterRoundAsync(results, cancellation.Token);` leaves every test green; the feature's one production entry point is unpinned. Only five test files mention QuotaCooldowns and none runs RoundEngine: S22–S25 call AfterRoundAsync directly, and S26–S29 write the file by hand. This breaks the testing rule that the line a user would miss must go red when deleted, and module_tests.md lists the flow as covered.
findings.fix: Add one scenario through PanelService/RoundEngine with a scripted launcher: an agy (or claude) row ends spent in round 1, then assert that quota-cooldowns.json holds the key and that ExcludedFrom / the next round's roster leaves the row out. Watch it go red with line 441 removed.

findings.summary: A cancellation in one key's probe throws out the changes already decided for every other key in the round: the catch returns before Apply, so a codex or claude park, or a lift, is lost too. Also, the token is RoundCancellation's, which fires on the round's own deadline, so a round that ended by its clock never parks an agy key (the launcher returns Cancelled, which becomes an OperationCanceledException).
findings.fix: Catch cancellation per key inside the loop, drop only that key's change, and still Apply the rest. Consider giving the probe a token tied only to the caller and host stop, not to the round clock.

findings.summary: Apply calls HeldFile.TakeWithin, a Thread.Sleep polling loop that can wait up to 30 s by default, and it is called synchronously from the async AfterRoundAsync. That blocks a thread-pool thread under contention, which common.reliability forbids ('A blocking lock is never taken directly on an async worker thread').
findings.fix: Take the lock off the async thread, as ConsultantPlaces.cs:125 does (Task.Run(() => HeldFile.TakeWithin(...), ct)), or give AfterRoundAsync an ApplyAsync that does.

findings.summary: AgyError.Parse reads stderr one line at a time, so the issue's own sample (#765, quoted verbatim in plan §1: `AGY_ERROR: {` followed by pretty-printed JSON over several lines) gives no error. The 'AGY_ERROR: {' line alone is not valid JSON, so that refusal falls back to the word scan with Spent null, and if /quota cannot be read the issue's exact case is never parked.
findings.fix: Parse the JSON object that starts after the token across the following lines (for example with Utf8JsonReader from the token's offset in the whole stderr), and add the #765 sample verbatim as an S4/S5 case.

findings.summary: S37's Then ('one notice naming it is handed to the notice writer') is proved only up to the onRefused callback. No test exercises QuotaNotices.Refused or PanelService's onRefused → Noticing.Offered wiring, yet module_tests.md says the notice road 'is proved by the notice's shape (QuotaNotices.Refused)'.
findings.fix: Add a test that a refused write through PanelService's store produces one storage-note notice with subject quota-cooldowns. Or correct the module_tests.md sentence to list it as not proved.

findings.summary: Two docs no longer match the code. §12's 'Open at the time of this status' bullet about the notice census is stale: commit 26bebc96 added QuotaNotices.cs to the census. And research/module_runners.md:1261 says the local record is lifted 'when a probe says it is free', but the code lifts only on an Ok answer (or at expiry) and never because of a probe.
findings.fix: Drop or rewrite the stale §12 bullet, and correct module_runners.md:1261 to say the record is lifted by an answered launch or by the clock.
